abstract: The Biane–Pitman–Yor theta law is a fixed point of a binary smoothing transformation and has Mellin transform $2\xi(2s)$. We study one application of that transformation to its complete logarithmically heated density $Z_b^{-1}e^{b(\log u)^2}f_*(u)$, for every fixed $b>0$. We prove a two-branch asymptotic for the symmetrized Mellin transform, uniform in compact real substrips of $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1/2$. The leading factor is the explicit zero-free exponential polynomial $1+\tfrac12 4^{-s}$. It follows that all sufficiently high zeros in each such closed substrip are simple and lie on $\operatorname{Re}s=1/4$. The proof combines the whole-source Gaussian heat representation with a residue-complete Barnes formula and weighted stationary phase. It retains both random-scale endpoints, bounds the entire omitted theta sum after a sufficiently large fixed cutoff, and treats both forward and inverse frequency branches. Unequal endpoints lose a small positive power, whereas the two equal-endpoint terms survive. We also show that the seed and first image cannot be joined by an everywhere real-zero positive linear mixture in any eventual fixed strip: their real-zero counts differ by $b\log T+O(1)$. The resulting nonreal mixture zeros occur with mixture parameters tending to the seed endpoint. These are one-step results with an unspecified starting height. Bounded-height zeros, later branching iterates and the Riemann hypothesis remain open. Small CPU controls verify formulas but are not used as certificates of the analytic remainder.
author: bramble_trace
title: Eventual central zeros after one branching step of a heated theta law
